title: Skill eval run record
description: Shape of the run record SKILL.md's Procedure step 7 writes when a gate run completes: one record per run, written into the target repository's own eval-results location, never an edit to an earlier one. This file pins shape only. What a run must capture is stated by that Procedure step, and the split is deliberate -- a corpus of records can validate individually against a schema and still drift into disagreeing key spellings and unreferenced attachments when no procedure ever says what to record. Additional keys are permitted: a run may carry its own extra context (a run-shape note, a pointer to a superseded record) without needing this schema widened, and a repository migrating pre-existing records onto this contract is doing its own work, not being retro-graded by this file.

date.description: The run's real calendar date, YYYY-MM-DD. Not a relative position in a git log, and not the date the record was tidied up.

issue.description: Full URL of the issue or change this run was performed for. A bare number is rejected by construction: it resolves only inside the repository that minted it, and a run record outlives that context.

commit.description: The exact commit the graded content was read at, as a hex object name. Without it a score cannot be re-derived, which is the whole point of recording one.

runner.description: The eval runner Procedure step 1 confirmed. Both fields come from the tool itself -- its own name and the version string it reported -- never from memory or from a toolchain pin read elsewhere.

name.description: The runner binary's name as invoked.

version.description: The version string the runner itself reported. A run that could not obtain one is not recorded here; step 1 stops instead.

fixture_set.description: Which fixtures ran and where their definitions live, specific enough that a reader can open them. A count alone does not satisfy this.

trials_per_fixture.description: How many trials each fixture got. One is a legitimate answer and a disclosed limit; zero is not a run.

models.description: Alias -> full model ID, covering every model actually invoked. Keyed by whatever alias the run used, valued by the full current identifier: an alias can re-resolve to a different underlying model over time, and a record that stored only the alias silently changes meaning when it does.

dispatch_mechanism.description: How the run was isolated from the authoring context. Whether isolation was actually achieved is a claim this field records and a reviewer checks; the schema can only require that the claim be made.

scorer.description: What produced the numbers -- the grader, checker, or script, named precisely enough to re-run.

score_files.description: One entry per model actually run, each pointing at that model's own score file. Named for the pointers it holds rather than for the scores themselves, which live one level down in those files under their own `scores` key (see eval-scores.schema.json) -- two differently-shaped lists sharing one key name is exactly the drift this contract exists to stop. A model listed in `models` with no entry here has no results and must be disclosed in `known_gaps` rather than left implied.

model_id.description: The full model ID, matching a value in `models`.

file.description: Path to this model's score file, relative to this record. Every attachment a run produces is reachable from here; an unreferenced file next to a record is an orphan, not a result.

known_gaps.description: The run's disclosed scope limits. Never omit this key to mean 'none': a run with nothing to disclose says so with a single explicit 'none known' entry, so a silent omission can never read as a clean run.

headline_pattern.description: A one-paragraph statement of the run's main finding, for a reader who will not open the score files.

supersedes.description: Optional. When this record corrects an earlier one, the earlier record it replaces. A correction is a new record naming its predecessor, never an edit to it.
